newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech official sees Norway gas deal decision soon.
newsitem.headline: Czech official sees Norway gas deal decision soon.

text.p: A senior official at the Czech Industry and Trade Ministry said on Tuesday that he expected the full Czech cabinet to decide next week on a long-term agreement for Norway to provide supplies of natural gas to the Czech Republic.

"My opinion is that (a final decision) will be (at) the next week's government meeting," Oldrich Petrzilka, the head of the ministry's gas industry division, told Reuters. "Negotiations are still being held on the price of the supplies."
A Norwegian industry ministry delegation accompanying Norway's King Harald on a state visit arrived in Prague on Tuesday.

Czech officials said Oslo's Industrial Affairs Minister Grete Knudsen began a meeting with Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy around midday. A joint news conference is scheduled for 1345 local time (1245 gmt).
Dlouhy said last week that Norway had been given priority out of four options for natural gas supplies in the Czechs' effort to diversify away from soley Russian gas.

"The contract that's being negotiated is a long-term contract...three billion cubic metres per year for 15 years, with the option of extension to 20 years," Petrzilka said. "In my opinion, the decision will be done in a week or 10 days."
The other options included potential deals with German, Dutch and British suppliers or a second delivery route of Russian gas.
Petrzilka added that alternative options to the Norwegian deal were still open should a final agreement with Oslo fail.
